deviations.what: All vLLM generations use Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8 (official block-FP8 checkpoint); every state, attention and CE readout uses bf16 Qwen/Qwen3-8B.
deviations.why: The pod has a 16 GB RTX 2000 Ada (not the planned 20 GB A4500): bf16 Qwen3-8B (16.4 GB of weights) does not fit in vLLM.
deviations.cost: Generated texts come from a quantised twin of the analysed model; FP8 can shift sampling probabilities slightly, so behavioural shares are not bit-comparable with iteration 1.

deviations.what: Fresh protocol-v2 ban pool: 20 runs per template (100 per task, 200 in total) instead of 40 per template (2 x 200).
deviations.why: Time lost to two interrupted sessions; vLLM runs on a 16 GB GPU with the FP8 twin.
deviations.cost: Wider CIs for readouts (i)-(iii); T1 has 15 BFS runs (all but 0 in W4) and T2 13 Dijkstra runs, so within-template AUCs rest mostly on W4 (T1) and W3/W4 (T2).

deviations.what: Same-seed CRN: 30 seeds (480 rows) instead of 50 (800 rows), per fallback F9 (cut seeds before conditions).
deviations.cost: Per-cell N = 30 (Wilson intervals reported); both conditions and all four temperatures kept.

deviations.what: Gumbel-max coupling sensitivity (Ravfogel et al. 2025) not run.
deviations.why: Drop order after the thought-anchor arm; time.
deviations.cost: The coupling-dependence of the CRN result is untested; the code path exists (vllm_stage.stage_gumbel).

deviations.what: The CRN sampler runs inside vLLM as a per-request logits processor (greedy decoding of a processor-chosen token) instead of a hand-written HF DynamicCache loop.
deviations.why: An HF decode loop over 800 rows does not fit the time budget on this GPU; the processor keeps the exact coupling (shared U[seed][t], inverse CDF over the (-logit, id)-sorted top-10).
deviations.cost: vLLM batches are not layout-controlled, so run-to-run identity is measured (determinism rerun + step-0 logits of identical histories) rather than guaranteed.

deviations.what: Thinking-on arms decode with Qwen3's recommended T=0.6 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 20.
deviations.why: Protocol T=1.0 targets thinking-off sampling; the recommended settings raise completion within the cap.
deviations.cost: Not directly comparable with exp6's T=1.0 thinking cells.

deviations.what: B2 layer-probe permutation null is computed for DiM only (200 within-paraphrase permutations); the full nested null for every method runs at the 3 chosen layers (B5).
deviations.why: A logistic-regression null at all 21 layers x 5 positions x 2 tasks is ~100x the CPU budget.
deviations.cost: Layer choice uses the DiM within-paraphrase AUC, as the rule specifies; no method's p-value at non-chosen layers is reported except DiM's.

deviations.what: HF readouts keep embed_tokens on the CPU and the Qwen-Scope SAE weights on the GPU in bf16 (fp32 pre-activations and top-k); attention rows come from a wrapped SDPA kernel.
deviations.why: bf16 Qwen3-8B (16.4 GB) plus a 2.1 GB fp32 SAE do not fit on the 16 GB GPU.
deviations.cost: SAE codes differ from fp32 codes by bf16 rounding of W_enc / W_dec; checked by FVU / relative MSE / spliced CE, and attention rows are checked against eager attention.

deviations.what: Thought anchors: 5 base traces per task (not 10), 4 resampled traces per task x 9 points x 6 continuations (432), chunked 384-token generation (<= 4 chunks), no adaptive top-up; validation completions reduced to 1 per resampled trace.
deviations.why: Thinking traces are long on this GPU (T1 traces think for 8.4k-9.3k tokens, ~50 tok/s aggregate).
deviations.cost: All 5 T1 traces exceed the 8,192-token thinking cap (complete=False by the plan's definition); 4 of them still close </think> and emit code, whose label is used as the reference outcome (flagged), else the early label.

deviations.what: SAE transfer corpus: exp1 stores only code, so each response is '```python\n' + code + '\n```' + <|im_end|>, as the plan's fallback says.
deviations.why: exp1 data/samples.jsonl has no full response text.
deviations.cost: Clean CE is very low (code-only responses are predictable); dCE ratios are still paired per sequence.

deviations.what: Figures are drawn with matplotlib directly (src/figures.py) from the results JSON files, not through the aii-data-fig-gen spec renderer.
deviations.cost: Same numbers, house style not applied.

deviations.what: J-lens applied directly from senku21x/cot-oracle-jlens lens.pt as lm_head(final_norm(J_l h)) without installing the jlens package; orientation (J h vs J^T h) chosen by the gate.
deviations.why: No time to vendor and pin the unmaintained reference package; the lens file holds the J matrices.
deviations.cost: If the reference 'unembed' differs from final-norm + lm_head, the gate result may understate the lens; the gate FAILED (J-lens top-1 agreement below the logit lens at every source layer), so J-lens readouts are descriptive only.

deviations.what: E2 attention rows are recomputed in fp32 from the SDPA query/key tensors for the k_pre / k_post queries only (no output_attentions); the eager comparison shows max |diff| <= 0.04 on 3 prompts (bf16 eager vs fp32 recomputation).
deviations.why: Eager attention with output_attentions for 600 forwards does not fit the 16 GB GPU budget alongside the model.
deviations.cost: Attention masses carry ~1e-2 numerical noise relative to bf16 eager attention.
